viii | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation FOREWORD The global rapid changes in the labour market tends to call for appropriate training and skills development through outcome-based training approaches. Skills development and employment promotion are central to Rwanda’s transformative Vision 2050, aiming to secure high standards of living for all Rwandans. In a bid to transform Rwanda into a knowledge based economy, the National Strategic Transformation 1(NST1) calls socio- economic transformation through TVET skills development. The Rwanda TVET Board (RTB) was established to promote quality education in technical and vocation education and training from level one (1) to five (5) aimed at fast tracking socio-economic development of the country. Designing and distributing curricula, teaching materials, trainer ’s guides, methodologies and establish training methods for technical and vocation education and training from level one (1) to five (5); is among other RTB’s responsibilities. The existing curricula were limited and narrowed in terms of acquired skills and knowledge and were not meeting the requirements of the current labour market at both national and regional level. In addition, there were barriers in vertical mobility and pathways in TVET which resulted in negative TVET perception. Furthermore, there were barriers to admission of TVET graduates in certain programs into higher learning institutions. The TVET modernization process has begun with a clear picture of the programs focusing on sector with the high employment potential like Building construction among others. In this respect, Rwanda TVET Board is honored to avail the revised Level 5 curriculum of Building Construction which serves as the official document and responds to the above-mentioned concerns. With the help of the training providers, trainers, parents whose role is central to the success of this curriculum, the trainees will gain appropriate hands on skills which will make a difference not only to their own lives but also to the success of Rwanda’s economy. I wish to sincerely extend my appreciation to the people who contributed towards the development of this document. Dip. -Eng. Paul UMUKUNZI Director General/ RTB

ix | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation 1. GENERAL INTRODUCTION The curriculum presents a coherent and significant set of competencies to perform the occupation of a Roof maker , Foreman , Scaffolder , Painter , Glazier , Cladding Installer and Ceiling Installer . It is designed with an approach that takes into account the training needs, the work situation, as well as the goals and the means to implement the training. The modules of the curriculum include a description of the expected results of the training. They have a direct influence on the choice of the theoretical and practical learning activities. The competencies are the targets of the training; the acquisition of each is required for certification. The curriculum is the reference to carry out the assessment of learning. Assessment tools of learning are developed based on this document. The curriculum consists of three parts: The first part is of general interest and shows the nature and goals of the program and the key concepts and definitions used in the document. The second part presents the qualification, its level in the qualification framework, its purpose, its rationale and the list of modules it comprises. The third part deals with the training package. It includes the competencies chart, the sequencing of module learning, the description of each module and the course structure. The pages describing the modules are the heart of a curriculum. They present the title of the module, the length of training, the amount of credits, the context in which the competency is performed, the prerequisite competencies, the learning outcomes and the performance criteria. In each module, a course structure is provided. The course structure describes the learning outcomes (knowledge, skills and attitudes) and the learning contents related to each learning outcome. In addition, the learning activities and resources for learning are suggested. Finally, the assessment specifications and guidelines are included in each module.

x | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation 1.1. Rationale of the Qualification Rwanda’s building and construction industry has rapidly grown in the past couple of years with both government and private sector engaged in the construction of buildings and roads infrastructure triggering what is now dubbed as a “construction boom in Rwanda”. The construction industry contributes immensely towards the GDP of the Country mainly through direct income and massive employment opportunities generated from various infrastructure projects, rehabilitation and maintenance. It is estimated that the construction sub-sector of the larger industrial sector contributes the highest to the country’s industrial GDP. However, there has been a shortage in skilled construction workers to work in the various for mentioned constructions. Additionally, there has been also an over dependence on imported building materials, which depletes the meager foreign exchange resources while denying the citizens the opportunities of production of the materials locally. In Rwanda, the available amounts of cement, granite, sand and stone are not fully exploited for industrial growth. The construction materials industry in Rwanda was profiled with a sampled analysis of eleven natural construction materials extractors, seven man-made products manufacturers and twelve contractors. The emerging issues highlight the following opportunities: vast quantities of natural construction materials, plenty of traditional knowledge in construction, a willing human resource, availability of construction industry related to technical institutions, regional integration and political will by the government to revitalize the industry. The constraints and weaknesses to development of this industry were identified as follows: an inefficient, inconsistent supply of raw materials, limited skilled manpower, capital-acquisition difficulties, high competition from other regional actors (from Kenya and Uganda), inconsistent and inadequate energy/power supply and low quality production output. Therefore, Roof maker , Foreman , Scaffolder , Painter , Glazier , Cladding Installer and Ceiling Installer , skilled are the key occupations that need to be trained to drive the target of the government in construction sector/Building Construction.

9 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation ASSESSMENT GUIDELINES 4.1 Assessment Methodology To assess knowledge, practical, and application skills through a jury system of continuous evaluation that encourages learners to display understanding of the principles in application to set practical tasks and their attendant theory to assess self-learning. There are two types of assessment (Formative Assessment and Summative/Integrated Assessment). Each assessment has its own rule for passing to be declared competent. Formative Assessment This is applied on all types of modules (e.g. Complementary, General and Specific modules) A trainee to be competent for a formative module must have at least 70% on checked items Or “yes” in indicators (e.g. questions, indicators in the checklist) Each trainee should be competent on all formative assessments to be declared competent on that module All formative assessment should be declared competent before taking the summative/integrated assessment.

10 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Summative/Integrated Assessment All Summative/Integrated assessment should match with the content of the module in the curriculum. Summative/Integrated Assessment is always in practical, giving it, as a theoretical type of assessment is not acceptable. The integrated situation provided in the curriculum is a sample of the assessment to be carried out, the Trainer/Teacher has the role of developing another one referring to the task to be carried out in the integrated situation in accordance to the circumstances inside school, but the integrated situation should stick on the components of a task. During Summative/Integrated assessment, assessor panel members should be three (3). The trainee can be declared competent based on the assessment CRITERIA and its respective assessment indicators The Passing Line for the modules is: ▪ 50 % for general and complementary modules ▪ 70 % for specific modules Training delivery 100% Assessment Total 100% Theoretical content 30% Formative assessment 30% 50% Practical work: 70% 70% Group project and presentation 20% Individual project /Work 50% Summative Assessment 50% Note: 1. Summative assessment is always conducted at the completion of module delivery. It should be practical through an integrated situation for specific modules and in any other forms of assessment for complementary and general modules. 2. Learning hours assigned to specific module includes the duration assigned to integrated assessment.

14 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation GLOSSARY 1. Competency-based assessment (or CBA): The gathering and judging of evidence in order to decide whether a person has achieved a standard of competency. 2. Complementary competencies : Set of knowledge, skills and attitudes which are not directly linked to a specific occupation or industry, but which are important for work, education and life in general, such as communication, mathematics, organizational aptitude, and computer literacy, interpersonal and analytical competency. 3. Core modules: Modules leading to competencies’ acquisition that an industry sector has agreed upon as essential for a person to be accepted as competent at a particular level. All modules may be core, but in many cases competency at a level will involve core modules plus optional or specialization modules. Core competencies are normally those central to work in a particular industry. 4. Credential: Formal certification issued for successful achievement of a defined set of outcomes, e.g. successful completion of a course in recognition of having achieved particular knowledge, skills or competencies; successful completion of an apprenticeship or traineeship. 5. Judging evidence in order to decide whether a person has attained a standard of performance. 6. Assessment criteria: Statements which describe performances and place them in context with sufficient precision to allow valid and reliable assessment. 7. Best practice: Management practices and work processes that lead to outstanding or top-class performance and provide examples for others. 8. Competency standard: An industry- determined specification of performance which sets out the skills, knowledge and attitudes required to operate effectively in employment. Competency standards are made up of units of competency, which are themselves made up of elements of competency, together with performance criteria, a range of variables, and an evidence guide. 9. Competency : means the ability to apply knowledge, skills and personal, social and methodological skills in the workplace or during learning, as well as in personal and professional development. This ability or capacity is acquired through leaning, exposure to the tasks and series of training allowing one to perform specific task autonomously. Reason why in the context of the CBE Framework competencies are described as responsibility and independence.

15 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation 10. Credit : The acknowledgement that a person has satisfied the requirements of a module. 11. Curriculum: The specifications for a course or subject (module) which describe all the learning experiences a learner undergoes, generally including objectives, content, intended learning outcomes, teaching methodology, recommended or prescribed assessment tasks, assessment exemplars, etc. 12. Evidence guide: The part of a competency standard which provides a guide to the interpretation and assessment of the unit of competency, including the aspects which need to be emphasized in assessment, relationships to other units, and the required evidence of competency. 13. Flexible delivery: A range of approaches to providing education and training, giving learners greater choice of when, where and how they learn. Flexible delivery may involve distance education, mixed-mode delivery, online education, self-paced learning, Self-directed learning, etc. 14. Formal education: Also, formal training education or training provided in educational institutions such as schools, universities, colleges, etc. or off the job in a workplace, usually involving direction from a teacher or instructor. 15. General competencies: competencies correspond to larger operations that go beyond the Tasks, but generally contribute to their implementation. These activities require more fundamental learning and are generally common to several tasks and transferable to many work situations. 16. Generic modules : Modules leading to the attainment of complementary competencies. 17. Informal education: The acquisition of knowledge and skills through experience, reading, social contact, etc. 18. Internship : An opportunity for a learner to integrate career related experience by participating in planned, supervised work. 19. Key competencies: Any of several generic skills or competencies considered essential for people to participate effectively in the workforce. Key competencies apply to work generally, rather than being specific to work in a particular occupation or industry. The following are key areas of competency which were developed into seven key competencies: collecting, analyzing and organizing information; communicating ideas and information; planning and organizing activities; working with others and in teams; using mathematical ideas and techniques; solving problems; and using technology. 20. Knowledge: means the result of the adoption of information through the learning process. Knowledge is a set of facts, principles, theories and practices

14 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Related to area of work or study. In CBE, context lifelong learning knowledge is described as theoretical and / or factual. 21. Learning outcomes : are statements of what learner knows, understands and can perform, based on the completion of the learning process, defined by knowledge, skill and competency. 22. Learning activities: Suggested activities that can be developed during lesson planning and activity preparation. The choice of learning activities must be tailored according to group size, available material resources and communication tools. 23. Learning hours: Amount of hours required to acquire the competency, including the time allocated to evaluation, which is estimated between 5 and 10% of the total learning time of the competency. 24. Learning outcomes: Statements that indicate what learners will know or be able to do as a result of a learning activity. Learning outcomes are usually expressed as knowledge, skills, or attitudes. 25. Learning unit: Any of the basic building blocks of a module, which describes the key activities or the elements of the work covered by the module 26. Module : A unit of training which corresponds to one competency and which can be completed on its own or linked to others. 27. Occupation : The principal business of one’s life. 28. Performance criteria The part of a competency standard specifying the required level of performance in terms of a set of outcomes which need to be achieved in order to be deemed competent. It describes the quality requirements of the result obtained in labor performance. 29. Qualification : means the formal name for the result of a process of assessment and validation, which is obtained when a competent body determines that an individual has achieved learning outcomes to the standards laid down. 30. Quality assurance: The systems and procedures designed and implemented by an organization to ensure that its products and services are of a consistent standard and are being continuously improved. 31. Recognition of prior learning (or RPL): The acknowledgement of a person’s skills and knowledge acquired through previous training, work or life experience, which may be used to grant status or credit in a subject or module. 32. Skills: are the ability to apply knowledge and use the principle of “know how” to perform a specific task and to solve the problem. In the context of the CBE Framework, skills are defined as cognitive (involving the use of logical, intuitive and creative thinking), practical (including physical skill and use of methods, materials, devices and instruments) and social skills (communication and cooperation

14 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Skills, emotional intelligence and other). 33. Specific competencies: Competencies that are directly related to the tasks of the occupation in the workplace context. They refer to concrete, practical, and focused aspects 34. Traineeship: A system of vocational training combining off- the-job training at an approved training provider with on-the-job training and practical work Experience. Traineeships generally take one to two years and are now a part of the New Apprenticeships system. 35. Unit of competency: A component of a competency standard. A unit of competency is a statement of a key function or role in a particular job or occupation. See also element of competency, performance criteria, range of variables.

viii | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation FOREWORD The global rapid changes in the labour market tends to call for appropriate training and skills development through outcome-based training approaches. Skills development and employment promotion are central to Rwanda’s transformative Vision 2050, aiming to secure high standards of living for all Rwandans. In a bid to transform Rwanda into a knowledge based economy, the National Strategic Transformation 1(NST1) calls socio- economic transformation through TVET skills development. The Rwanda TVET Board (RTB) was established to promote quality education in technical and vocation education and training from level one (1) to five (5) aimed at fast tracking socio-economic development of the country. Designing and distributing curricula, teaching materials, trainer ’s guides, methodologies and establish training methods for technical and vocation education and training from level one (1) to five (5); is among other RTB’s responsibilities. The existing curricula were limited and narrowed in terms of acquired skills and knowledge and were not meeting the requirements of the current labour market at both national and regional level. In addition, there were barriers in vertical mobility and pathways in TVET which resulted in negative TVET perception. Furthermore, there were barriers to admission of TVET graduates in certain programs into higher learning institutions. The TVET modernization process has begun with a clear picture of the programs focusing on sector with the high employment potential like Building construction among others. In this respect, Rwanda TVET Board is honored to avail the revised Level 5 curriculum of Building Construction which serves as the official document and responds to the above-mentioned concerns. With the help of the training providers, trainers, parents whose role is central to the success of this curriculum, the trainees will gain appropriate hands on skills which will make a difference not only to their own lives but also to the success of Rwanda’s economy. I wish to sincerely extend my appreciation to the people who contributed towards the development of this document. Dip. -Eng. Paul UMUKUNZI Director General/ RTB
ix | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation 1. GENERAL INTRODUCTION The curriculum presents a coherent and significant set of competencies to perform the occupation of a Roof maker , Foreman , Scaffolder , Painter , Glazier , Cladding Installer and Ceiling Installer . It is designed with an approach that takes into account the training needs, the work situation, as well as the goals and the means to implement the training. The modules of the curriculum include a description of the expected results of the training. They have a direct influence on the choice of the theoretical and practical learning activities. The competencies are the targets of the training; the acquisition of each is required for certification. The curriculum is the reference to carry out the assessment of learning. Assessment tools of learning are developed based on this document. The curriculum consists of three parts: The first part is of general interest and shows the nature and goals of the program and the key concepts and definitions used in the document. The second part presents the qualification, its level in the qualification framework, its purpose, its rationale and the list of modules it comprises. The third part deals with the training package. It includes the competencies chart, the sequencing of module learning, the description of each module and the course structure. The pages describing the modules are the heart of a curriculum. They present the title of the module, the length of training, the amount of credits, the context in which the competency is performed, the prerequisite competencies, the learning outcomes and the performance criteria. In each module, a course structure is provided. The course structure describes the learning outcomes (knowledge, skills and attitudes) and the learning contents related to each learning outcome. In addition, the learning activities and resources for learning are suggested. Finally, the assessment specifications and guidelines are included in each module.
x | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation 1.1. Rationale of the Qualification Rwanda’s building and construction industry has rapidly grown in the past couple of years with both government and private sector engaged in the construction of buildings and roads infrastructure triggering what is now dubbed as a “construction boom in Rwanda”. The construction industry contributes immensely towards the GDP of the Country mainly through direct income and massive employment opportunities generated from various infrastructure projects, rehabilitation and maintenance. It is estimated that the construction sub-sector of the larger industrial sector contributes the highest to the country’s industrial GDP. However, there has been a shortage in skilled construction workers to work in the various for mentioned constructions. Additionally, there has been also an over dependence on imported building materials, which depletes the meager foreign exchange resources while denying the citizens the opportunities of production of the materials locally. In Rwanda, the available amounts of cement, granite, sand and stone are not fully exploited for industrial growth. The construction materials industry in Rwanda was profiled with a sampled analysis of eleven natural construction materials extractors, seven man-made products manufacturers and twelve contractors. The emerging issues highlight the following opportunities: vast quantities of natural construction materials, plenty of traditional knowledge in construction, a willing human resource, availability of construction industry related to technical institutions, regional integration and political will by the government to revitalize the industry. The constraints and weaknesses to development of this industry were identified as follows: an inefficient, inconsistent supply of raw materials, limited skilled manpower, capital-acquisition difficulties, high competition from other regional actors (from Kenya and Uganda), inconsistent and inadequate energy/power supply and low quality production output. Therefore, Roof maker , Foreman , Scaffolder , Painter , Glazier , Cladding Installer and Ceiling Installer , skilled are the key occupations that need to be trained to drive the target of the government in construction sector/Building Construction.

14 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation GLOSSARY 1. Competency-based assessment (or CBA): The gathering and judging of evidence in order to decide whether a person has achieved a standard of competency. 2. Complementary competencies : Set of knowledge, skills and attitudes which are not directly linked to a specific occupation or industry, but which are important for work, education and life in general, such as communication, mathematics, organizational aptitude, and computer literacy, interpersonal and analytical competency. 3. Core modules: Modules leading to competencies’ acquisition that an industry sector has agreed upon as essential for a person to be accepted as competent at a particular level. All modules may be core, but in many cases competency at a level will involve core modules plus optional or specialization modules. Core competencies are normally those central to work in a particular industry. 4. Credential: Formal certification issued for successful achievement of a defined set of outcomes, e.g. successful completion of a course in recognition of having achieved particular knowledge, skills or competencies; successful completion of an apprenticeship or traineeship. 5. Judging evidence in order to decide whether a person has attained a standard of performance. 6. Assessment criteria: Statements which describe performances and place them in context with sufficient precision to allow valid and reliable assessment. 7. Best practice: Management practices and work processes that lead to outstanding or top-class performance and provide examples for others. 8. Competency standard: An industry- determined specification of performance which sets out the skills, knowledge and attitudes required to operate effectively in employment. Competency standards are made up of units of competency, which are themselves made up of elements of competency, together with performance criteria, a range of variables, and an evidence guide. 9. Competency : means the ability to apply knowledge, skills and personal, social and methodological skills in the workplace or during learning, as well as in personal and professional development. This ability or capacity is acquired through leaning, exposure to the tasks and series of training allowing one to perform specific task autonomously. Reason why in the context of the CBE Framework competencies are described as responsibility and independence.
15 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation 10. Credit : The acknowledgement that a person has satisfied the requirements of a module. 11. Curriculum: The specifications for a course or subject (module) which describe all the learning experiences a learner undergoes, generally including objectives, content, intended learning outcomes, teaching methodology, recommended or prescribed assessment tasks, assessment exemplars, etc. 12. Evidence guide: The part of a competency standard which provides a guide to the interpretation and assessment of the unit of competency, including the aspects which need to be emphasized in assessment, relationships to other units, and the required evidence of competency. 13. Flexible delivery: A range of approaches to providing education and training, giving learners greater choice of when, where and how they learn. Flexible delivery may involve distance education, mixed-mode delivery, online education, self-paced learning, Self-directed learning, etc. 14. Formal education: Also, formal training education or training provided in educational institutions such as schools, universities, colleges, etc. or off the job in a workplace, usually involving direction from a teacher or instructor. 15. General competencies: competencies correspond to larger operations that go beyond the Tasks, but generally contribute to their implementation. These activities require more fundamental learning and are generally common to several tasks and transferable to many work situations. 16. Generic modules : Modules leading to the attainment of complementary competencies. 17. Informal education: The acquisition of knowledge and skills through experience, reading, social contact, etc. 18. Internship : An opportunity for a learner to integrate career related experience by participating in planned, supervised work. 19. Key competencies: Any of several generic skills or competencies considered essential for people to participate effectively in the workforce. Key competencies apply to work generally, rather than being specific to work in a particular occupation or industry. The following are key areas of competency which were developed into seven key competencies: collecting, analyzing and organizing information; communicating ideas and information; planning and organizing activities; working with others and in teams; using mathematical ideas and techniques; solving problems; and using technology. 20. Knowledge: means the result of the adoption of information through the learning process. Knowledge is a set of facts, principles, theories and practices
14 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Related to area of work or study. In CBE, context lifelong learning knowledge is described as theoretical and / or factual. 21. Learning outcomes : are statements of what learner knows, understands and can perform, based on the completion of the learning process, defined by knowledge, skill and competency. 22. Learning activities: Suggested activities that can be developed during lesson planning and activity preparation. The choice of learning activities must be tailored according to group size, available material resources and communication tools. 23. Learning hours: Amount of hours required to acquire the competency, including the time allocated to evaluation, which is estimated between 5 and 10% of the total learning time of the competency. 24. Learning outcomes: Statements that indicate what learners will know or be able to do as a result of a learning activity. Learning outcomes are usually expressed as knowledge, skills, or attitudes. 25. Learning unit: Any of the basic building blocks of a module, which describes the key activities or the elements of the work covered by the module 26. Module : A unit of training which corresponds to one competency and which can be completed on its own or linked to others. 27. Occupation : The principal business of one’s life. 28. Performance criteria The part of a competency standard specifying the required level of performance in terms of a set of outcomes which need to be achieved in order to be deemed competent. It describes the quality requirements of the result obtained in labor performance. 29. Qualification : means the formal name for the result of a process of assessment and validation, which is obtained when a competent body determines that an individual has achieved learning outcomes to the standards laid down. 30. Quality assurance: The systems and procedures designed and implemented by an organization to ensure that its products and services are of a consistent standard and are being continuously improved. 31. Recognition of prior learning (or RPL): The acknowledgement of a person’s skills and knowledge acquired through previous training, work or life experience, which may be used to grant status or credit in a subject or module. 32. Skills: are the ability to apply knowledge and use the principle of “know how” to perform a specific task and to solve the problem. In the context of the CBE Framework, skills are defined as cognitive (involving the use of logical, intuitive and creative thinking), practical (including physical skill and use of methods, materials, devices and instruments) and social skills (communication and cooperation
14 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Skills, emotional intelligence and other). 33. Specific competencies: Competencies that are directly related to the tasks of the occupation in the workplace context. They refer to concrete, practical, and focused aspects 34. Traineeship: A system of vocational training combining off- the-job training at an approved training provider with on-the-job training and practical work Experience. Traineeships generally take one to two years and are now a part of the New Apprenticeships system. 35. Unit of competency: A component of a competency standard. A unit of competency is a statement of a key function or role in a particular job or occupation. See also element of competency, performance criteria, range of variables.

It is meant for learners who have successfully completed level IV in building construction and pursuing level V in building construction. At the end of this module, learners will be able to manage construction site documents, Conduct the management of construction activities, Prepare and manage contract with minimum supervision. pages.text: BDCPC301 - APPLY BASICS OF ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY Competence GENAC502 RQF Level: 5 Learning Hours 30 Credits: 3 Sector: Building and construction services, Agriculture and food processing, Transport and logistics, Manufacturing and mining, Hospitality tourism, Art and craft. Trade: Building construction, Public works, Land surveying, Plumbing Technology, Interior design, Agriculture, Animal health, Wood Technology, Leather technology, Forestry, Water and Irrigation, Food processing, Automobile technology, Heavy machinery, Manufacturing technology, Mining technology, Food and beverages operations, Fine and plastic arts. Module Type: General Curriculum: TVET Certificate 5 in Building construction, public works, Land surveying, Plumbing Technology, Interior design, Agriculture, Animal health, Wood Technology, Leather technology, Forestry, Water and Irrigation, Food processing, Automobile technology, Heavy machinery, Manufacturing technology, Mining technology, Food and beverage operations, Fine and plastic arts. Copyright: © Rwanda TVET Board, 2023 2024/25 Issue Date: May 2023

1 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Purpose statement This module describes the knowledge, skills and attitudes required to explain the introduction to Analytical Chemistry. At the end of this module, the learner will be able to differentiate qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis, discuss solubility and describe the electrochemical cell reactions. Delivery modality Training delivery 100% Assessment Total 100% Theoretical content 30% Formative assessment 30% 50% Practical work: 70% 70% • Group project and presentation 20% • Individual project /Work 50% Summative Assessment 50% Elements of Competency and Performance Criteria Elements of competency Performance criteria 1. Differentiate qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis 1.1. Qualitative chemical analysis is clearly explained based on its methods 1.2. Quantitative chemical analysis is properly explained based on its methods 1.3. Applications of chemical analysis are correctly discussed based on the areas of application 2. Discuss solubility 2.1. Solubility factors are properly identified according to the nature of solution 2.2. Solubility product is correctly explained based on the nature of salt 2.3. Solubility product is accurately calculated according to the solubility equilibrium 3. Describe the electrochemical cell reactions 3.1. Electrolysis is clearly explained according to Faraday’s Law 3.2. Electrochemical cells are properly illustrated according to redox half-cell reactions 3.3. Overall energy of electrochemical cell is accurately determined based on the half- cell reactions

2 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Course content Learning outcomes At the end of the module the learner will be able to: 1. Differentiate qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis 2. Discuss solubility 3. Describe the electrochemical cell reactions Learning outcome 1: Differentiate qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis Learning hours: 10 Indicative content • Definition of key terms ✓ Analytical chemistry ✓ Qualitative chemical analysis ✓ Quantitative chemical analysis • Explanation of qualitative chemical analysis ✓ Types of qualitative methods Flame test Distillation Extraction Precipitation ✓ Factors/criteria considered for qualitative chemical analysis Colour Odour Melting point Boiling point Solubility Radioactivity/Reactivity • Explanation of quantitative chemical analysis ✓ Quantitative methods Volumetric method/Titration Gravimetric method • Applications of chemical analysis ✓ Water analysis ✓ Soil analysis ✓ Food analysis ✓ Pharmaceuticals analysis ✓ Fertilizers and pesticides

3 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Resources required for the learning outcome Equipment - White/black board, projector, computer, chalkboard, DVD players, Bunsen burner Materials - Reference books, marker pen, flip chalks, chart, Metals (Ca, Mg, Na, Cu, P), salts (CaSO 4, BaSO 4, AgBr), H 2 O. Tools - Internet connection, platinum wire, nickel-chromium wire, beakers, conical flasks, balance Facilitation techniques - Demonstration and simulation, individual and group work, individualized, group discussion Formative assessment methods - Written assessment, oral presentation, performance assessment, product-based assessment Learning outcome 2: Discuss solubility Learning hours: 10 Indicative content • Explanation solubility ✓ Solubility ✓ Soluble, insoluble and sparingly soluble salts ✓ Solubility rules • Identification of factors affecting solubility of salts ✓ Temperature ✓ Pressure ✓ Polarity ✓ Molecular size of solute • Explanation of the solubility product ✓ Types of solution Unsaturated Saturated Supersaturated ✓ Dissociation of sparingly soluble salts in water Dissociation equation Expression of solubility product • Calculation of the solubility product ✓ Relationship between solubility and solubility product ✓ Applications of solubility Resources required for the indicative content

4 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Equipment - White/black board, projector, computer, chalkboard, DVD players Materials - Reference books, marker pen, flip chalks, chart, chemical salts, sugar, sand Tools - Internet connection, laboratory apparatus Facilitation techniques - Lectures, demonstration and simulation, individual and group work, practical exercise, individualized, trainer guided, group discussion Formative assessment methods - Written assessment, oral presentation, performance assessment, product based assessment, project based assessment Learning outcome 3: Describe the electrochemical cell reactions Learning hours: 10 Indicative content • Explanation of electrolysis ✓ Key terms Electrochemistry Electrolysis ✓ Electrolytic cell Components of electrolytic cell (electrodes, electrolyte and electricity) Diagram Working principle Faraday’s law ✓ Applications of electrolysis Production of chemicals (Na, Cl 2 , H 2 , … ) Electroplating Electrometallurgy (metal extraction) Metal refining (purification) • Illustrate electrochemical cell (galvanic cell) ✓ Electrochemical cell ✓ General representation of electrochemical cell ✓ Types of batteries Primary batteries Secondary batteries • Determination of electromotive force of the cell ✓ Electrochemical cell reactions Oxidation and reduction reaction ✓ Standard Electrode Potential (SEP)

5 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Table of Standard Electrode Potential (SEP) ✓ Electrode potential/electromotive force (E 0 ) Anodic and cathodic potential Overall potential of the cell Resources required for the indicative content Equipment - White/black board, projector, computer, chalkboard, DVD players, battery. Materials - marker pen, flip chalks, chart, NaCl, distilled water, Tools - Reference books, internet connection, laboratory apparatus, connecting wires, electrodes, electrochemical cell. Facilitation techniques - Lectures, demonstration and simulation, individual and group work, practical exercise, individualized, trainer guided, group discussion Formative assessment methods - Written assessment, oral presentation, performance assessment, product- based assessment.

pages.text: Apply ArchiCAD Software Competence BDCAC501 RQF Level: 5 Learning Hours 70 Credits: 7 Sector: Construction and Building Services Trade: Building Construction Module Type: Specific Curriculum: CBSBDC5001-TVET Certificate V in Building Construction Copyright: © Rwanda TVET Board, 2024 Issue Date: May 2024 2024-25

Purpose statement This specific module describes the skills, knowledge, and attitudes required to use ArchiCAD software. It is meant for learners who have successfully completed level IV in building construction and pursuing level V in building construction. At the end of this module, learners will be able to prepare the ArchiCAD software environment, produce ArchiCAD drawings, and print out ArchiCAD drawings. Learning assumed to be in place N/A Delivery modality Training delivery 100% Assessment Total 100% Theoretical content 30% Formative assessment 30% 50% Practical work: 70% 70% • Group project and presentation 20% • Individual project /Work 50% Summative Assessment 50% Elements of Competency and Performance Criteria Elements of competency Performance criteria Prepare ArchiCAD software environment 1.1 ArchiCAD software requirements are properly analyzed based on the operating system 1.2 ArchiCAD software is properly installed based on the Operating System 1.3 Software is properly customized as per the installation user guide Produce ArchiCAD Drawings 2.1 Project units are properly set up according to the scale of the drawing 2.2 Software tools are Appropriately used according to the design objectives 2.3 Software 2D drawings are appropriately created according to desired design 2.4 Software 3D modeling is appropriately created according to desired design 2.5 Title block is appropriately created according to the standard requirements Print out ArchiCAD drawings 3.1 Master layout book is appropriately created according to the scale of the drawing 3.2 Placing Views on the layout is placed on layout in accordance to scale of drawing 3.3 Project layout is appropriately saved according to the given project

2 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation 3.4 Layout books are appropriately printed out according to the required document format. Intended Knowledge, Skills and Attitude Knowledge Skills Attitude ✓ Describe architectural design principles and theories ✓ Identify building materials ✓ Describe construction methods and building services ✓ Describe the ArchiCAD software's capabilities, features, and limitations ✓ Identify building codes, regulations, and industry standards ✓ Describe construction documentation ✓ Identify industry trends, emerging technologies, and software updates ✓ Perform ArchiCAD installation ✓ Produce 2D drawings such as plans, sections, and elevations ✓ Produce 3D drawings such as perspectives. ✓ Perform navigation in ArchiCAD software. ✓ Use ArchiCAD design tools ✓ Perform high-quality visualizations and renderings ✓ Integrate ArchiCAD with other design and analysis software ✓ Print out a drawing ✓ Make continuous learning and skill development ✓ Pay attention to detail and precision in design and documentation ✓ Adapt to software updates and industry requirements ✓ Aware of collaborative mindset for effective coordination with project stakeholders ✓ Proactive to problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities ✓ Willing to experiment and explore new design possibilities ✓ Effective time management and organizational skills ✓ Conduct ethical and professional architectural practice

3 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Course content Learning outcomes At the end of the module the learner will be able to: 1. Prepare ArchiCAD software environment 2. Produce ArchiCAD Drawings 3. Print out ArchiCAD drawings Learning outcome 1: Prepare ArchiCAD Software Environment Learning hours: 10 Indicative content • Analysing ArchiCAD software requirements ✓ Description of ArchiCAD : History Advantages Applications Features ✓ Identification of ArchiCAD requirements ✓ Introduction to Building Information Modelling (BIM) system History interoperability ✓ Interacting ArchiCAD and Building information modeling (BIM) system Create Model Integrating Data Collaboration Detecting Clash Quantity take-off • Installation of ArchiCAD Software ✓ Run the installation file ✓ Activate your ArchiCAD license ✓ Configure ArchiCAD settings • Customization ArchiCAD Software ✓ Set Up Work Environment ✓ Configuration Project Templates ✓ Library Management ✓ Use shortcut keys Resources required for the indicative content Equipment • Computer, projector, Whiteboard Materials • flip chart, mark pens, Duster, Chalks, Papers

4 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Tools • Mouse and mouse mat, Electrical cables, - Storage devices (flash disc, CD, External disk), Software protocols, ArchiCAD software Facilitation techniques Group discussions, Simulations, Scenario, Trainer Guided • The trainer asks the students to discuss on the ArchiCAD software requirements and building information modelling. The trainer presents the inter relationship of both ARCHICAD and BIM • The trainer introduces the software installation file to students, demonstrate how to install the ArchiCAD software putting in consideration the software license and settings, and asks the students to follow the procedures. • The trainer shares the software file to students in manageable groups and the students practise the exercise of installing the software • The trainer through the installed software demonstrates how to set up work environment, configure project templates, library management and how to use shortcut keys and create architectural drawings asks the students to follow the procedure. • In manageable groups, the trainer asks the students to discuss on setting up work environment, configure project templates and practise use of shortcuts. • The trainer provides an expert view after each presentation. Formative assessment methods • Written assessment • Oral assessment • Practical assessment Learning outcome 2: Produce ArchiCAD drawings Learning hours: 50 Indicative content • Set up project units ✓ Selecting option menu ✓ Selecting project preferences • Using Software tools ✓ Identification of ArchiCAD tools Design Tools Documentation Tools Visualization Tools Modelling Tools Collaboration Tools Visualization & Rendering Analytical Tools Automation & Customization Library & Object Management Site Tools

5 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation ✓ Applying software tools • Creating 2D drawings ✓ Produce 2D Plan views ✓ Make cross-section views ✓ Make elevation views • Creating 3D modelling ✓ Set 3D projections ✓ Set 3D rendering ✓ Generate 3D perspectives • Creating title block ✓ Select layout book ✓ Create a new master layout ✓ Define paper size ✓ Drawing title block elements Resources required for the indicative content Equipment • Computer, projector, Whiteboard Materials • flip chart, mark pens, Duster, Chalks, Papers Tools • Mouse and mouse mat, Board, Electrical cables, - Storage devices, (flash disc, CD, External disk), Software protocols, and software video tutorials Facilitation techniques Group discussions, Simulations, Scenario, Trainer guided • The trainer demonstrates to the students how to set up project units, using software tools and asks the student to follow the procedures • Trainer demonstrate to the students the way applying ArchiCAD software tools used to produce drawings and asks the students to follow the procedure. • The trainer provides practical exercises on analyzing and interpreting produced ArchiCAD softcopy drawing documents. • Trainer forms small and manageable groups of students and asks the respective groups to discuss on ArchiCAD Software tools in the creation of 2D and 3D architectural drawings. • The trainer provides enough time to practice what has been taught by giving students different practices, different reference tutorial videos and asking them to present the 2D and 3D architectural drawings. • After submitting, each and every presentation, the trainer provides an expert view of the presented works Formative assessment methods • Written assessment • Oral assessment • Practical assessment

6 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Learning outcome 3: Print out ArchiCAD Drawings Learning hours: 10 Indicative content • Creating Master layout book ✓ Identification of the paper sizes of the master layout ✓ Description of a paper size appropriate for drawing ✓ Adjustment of paper size and scale ✓ Allocating Title block • Placing Views on the layout ✓ Drag and place 2D views ✓ Drag and place 3D views ✓ Adjusting View Settings • Saving Project layout ✓ Select master layout ✓ Select the file menu ✓ Choose file formats • Printing of layout books ✓ Review published or exported PDF drawings ✓ Print drawings ✓ Check hardcopy drawings Resources required for the indicative content Equipment - Computer, projector , whiteboard, printer Materials Flip chart, mark pens, duster, chalks, papers, printer ink Tools Mouse and mouse mat, board, electrical cables, - storage devices, (flash disc, CD, external disk), software protocols Facilitation techniques Assimilation, Group discussions, Trainer guided • The trainer asks the students to discuss on the paper size of the master layout and present the expert view • The trainer illustrates on the software how to create master layout book, choose & adjust the size and insert the tittle block with complete relevant information and finally name the master lay • Trainer demonstrate to the students to create master layout book and asks the students to follow the procedures. • The trainer demonstrate to the students how to drag and place the 2D & 3D architectural drawings to the master layout and asks the student to follow the procedures. • The trainer demonstrate to the students how to save these projects in portable document format (PDF) or any other formats compatible to ARCHICAD software and asks the student to follow the procedure.

7 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation • The trainer tasks each and every student to save their respective project architectural drawings in in portable document format (PDF) or any other formats compatible to ARCHICAD software , this is done by trainee’s as he/she monitors. • The trainer uses the saved architectural drawings saved in (PDF) or any other formats compatible to ARCHICAD software to review and further elaborates on how to adjust printing settings in accordance to the size of choice. Formative assessment methods • Written assessment • Oral assessment • Practical assessment

8 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Integrated/Summative assessment (For specific module) Integrated situation ABC Ltd company has won a contract to conduct an architectural study of a Two (2) storied classroom building in the Nyanza district. The contract scope is about producing and availing all architectural drawings of the building for future construction and permit request processes. Each floor is composed of eight (8) office rooms, one (1) medium hall, four toilet rooms, and one (1) teacher’s room . As a designer and employee of the company, you are requested to conduct this study and produce all required architectural drawings in a period not later than three (5) hours. The final drawings will be orally presented after their submission. Consider the following information: ✓ All stories are similar ✓ The playground is from the side of the building. ✓ The teacher’s room is at the entrance of the first floor ✓ The building will have a staircase. ✓ The toilets are located on the other side with natural ventilation Resources: Tools Mouse and mouse mat, Electrical cables, - Storage devices, (flash disc, CD, External disk), pencils Equipment Computer, Printer Materials/ Consumables Papers, printer ink Assessable outcomes Assessment criteria (Based on performance criteria) Indicator Observation Marks allocati on Yes No Learning outcome 1: Prepare ArchiCAD software environment ArchiCAD software is properly installed based on the Operating System installation file is installed 2 ArchiCAD license is Activated 2 ArchiCAD settings are Configured 2 Software is properly customized as per the installation user guide Work Environment is Settled Up 2 Project Templates Configured 2 Library is Managed 2 shortcut keys are Used 2 Learning outcome 2: Produce Project units are properly set up according to the scale of the drawing working units are Chosen 4 scale is Chosen 3 Working area are respected 2

Plan views are designed 4 Section views are designed 4 Elevation views are designed 4 Software 3D modeling is appropriately created according to the desired design 3D Navigation are applied 4 3D rendering are applied 4 Title block is appropriately created according to the standard requirements Layout book is selected 4 New master layout is created 3 Paper sizes are defined 3 Title blocks elements are drawn 2 Learning Outcome 3: Print out ArchiCAD drawings Master layout book is appropriately created according to the scale of the drawing Paper size and scales are properly adjusted 3 Title block is allocated 3 Views are correctly saved and placed on the layout in accordance with to scale of a drawing 2D Views are Dragged and placed 4 3D Views are Dragged and placed 2 View settings are Adjusted 2 Project layout is appropriately saved according to the given project Master layout is Select 2 file menu is Selected 2 file formats are Chosen 2 PDF drawings are exported 2

pages.text: Perform Acoustic and Thermal Insulations Competence BDCAT501 RQF Level: 5 Learning Hours 60 Credits: 6 Sector: Construction and Building Services Trade: Building Construction Module Type: specific Curriculum: CBSBDC5001- TVET Certificate 5 in Building Construction Copyright: © Rwanda TVET Board, 2024 Issue Date: May 2024 2024-25

1 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Purpose statement This specific module describes the knowledge, skills, and attitude of performing acoustic and thermal insulation works. It is intended to be pursued by the learners at TVET Certificate V in building construction. At the end of this module, the learner will be able to perform preliminary works, construct soundproof elements, and install thermal insulation panels. Learning assumed to be in place Roof Construction, Ceiling Installation, Basic Reinforced Concrete Design, Scaffolding Operation, ARCHICAD software, Applied Physics Delivery modality Training delivery 100% Assessment Total 100% Theoretical content 30% Formative assessment 30% 50% Practical work: 70% 70% • Group project and presentation 20% • Individual project /Work 50% Summative Assessment 50% Elements of Competency and Performance Criteria Elements of competency Performance criteria 1. Perform preliminary works 1.1. Sound and thermal insulation requirements are identified based on the usage of the building 1.2. Materials, tools, and equipment are appropriately selected in accordance to the project acoustic insulation specifications. 1.3. Materials, tools, and equipment are appropriately selected in accordance to the project thermal insulation specifications. 1.4. Working place is properly prepared based on-site conditions and type of insulation 2. Construct sound proof elements 2.1. 1 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Purpose statement This specific module describes the skills, knowledge and attitude to perform reinforced concrete works on construction site. It is intended to be pursued by learner at TVET level V for TVET Certificate IV in Building Construction. At the end of this module, the learner will be able to: Interpret structural details, identify structural members’ connections, determine forces acting on structural members and design concrete structure elements. Leaning assumed to be in place N/A Delivery modality Training delivery 100% Assessment Total 100% Theoretical content 30% Formative assessment 30% 50% Practical work: 70% 70% ➢ Group project and presentation 20% ➢ Individual project /Work 50% Summative Assessment 50% Elements of Competency and Performance Criteria Elements of competency Performance criteria 1. Structural members' details are correctly interpreted according to their types 1.3. Structural members section is correctly interpreted based on the structural details. 1.4. Bar bending schedules are correctly interpreted according to the type and form of structural member 2. Identify structural members connections 2.1. Reinforced concrete members are correctly positioned according to the construction structural drawings 2.2. Reinforced concrete members interconnections are adequately identified according to the construction drawings 2.3. Structure ’s supports are adequately identified based on the type of connections 2.4. Support reactions are correctly identified based on the type of connections

Design concrete structure elements 4.1. Internal forces are correctly determined based on applied loads. 4.2. Reinforced concrete design methods are properly used according to the structural member to be designed. 4.3. Serviceability of reinforced concrete design is adequately determined according to the structural member service 4.4. Reinforced concrete beam is correctly designed according to applied loads 4.5. Reinforced concrete slab is correctly designed according to applied loads 4.6. Reinforced concrete column is correctly designed according to applied loads 4.7. 1 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Purpose statement This specific module describes the skills, knowledge and attitudes required to construct ceiling. It is meant for learners who have successfully completed level IV in building construction and pursuing level V in building construction. At the end of this module students will be able to Perform ceiling preliminary works, set out ceiling, construct ceiling frame and apply ceiling coverings with minimum supervision. Leaning assumed to be in place scaffolding operations, Roof construction, ARCHICAD software Delivery modality Training delivery 100% Assessment Total 100% Theoretical content 30% Formative assessment 30% 50% Practical work: 70% 70% • Group project and presentation 20% • Individual project /Work 50% Summative Assessment 50% Elements of Competency and Performance Criteria Elements of competency Performance criteria Perform ceiling preliminary works 1.1 Ceiling drawings are properly interpreted according to the provided model. 1.2 Materials, tools and equipment are properly prepared based on ceiling type and its details. 1.3 Safety precautions are effectively applied according to the working condition. Set out ceiling frame 2.1 Reference line is correctly set according to construction drawing details 2.2 Height of the ceiling is correctly fixed based on type of ceiling 2.3 Level of ceiling and frame are precisely marked according to the type of ceiling 2.4 Level of frame ceiling is properly fixed according to the type of ceiling

2 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Construct ceiling frame 3.1 Scaffolding structure is properly erected according to the work to be performed 3.2 Ceiling frame layouts is properly identified based on ceiling drawing 3.3 Ceiling frame members are properly assembled based on the frame layouts Install ceiling covering materials 4.1. Ceiling panels are properly cut based on cutting lists 4.2. Ceiling panels are rigidly fixed to the frame based on ceiling drawing 4.3. Finishing works are properly performed in accordance with design concept Intended Knowledge, Skills and Attitude Knowledge Skills Attitude ✓ Identify types of ceiling ✓ Describe ceiling design principles ✓ Identify materials, tools and equipment used in ceiling ✓ Describe ceiling construction techniques ✓ Identify ceiling finishes ✓ Identify design tools ✓ Describe ceiling features ✓ Describe safety measures ✓ Describe project reports ✓ Perform ceiling cutting methods ✓ Interpret ceiling drawings ✓ Prepare ceiling boards panels ✓ Perform ceiling assembling techniques ✓ Fix ceiling members ✓ Carry out ceiling finishing activities ✓ Install the ceiling frame ✓ Apply ceiling construction procedures ✓ Use materials efficiently and effectively ✓ Make right decision within project design and execution ✓ Work under unexpected timeframe and conditions ✓ Pay attention to ceiling design project details ✓ Work collaboratively with team ✓ Use resources effectively during ceiling construction

3 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation ✓ Prepare ceiling project reports ✓ Use creativity and innovation throughout ceiling creation ✓ Meet set ceiling project deadlines ✓ Focus on ceiling project perfection Course content Learning outcomes At the end of the module the learner will be able to: 1. Perform ceiling preliminary works 2. Set out ceiling frame 3. Construct Ceiling frame 4. Apply ceiling covering Learning outcome 1: Perform ceiling preliminary works Learning hours: 5 hours Indicative content • Interpretation of ceiling drawings ✓ Drawing dimensions ✓ Drawing symbols and signs ✓ Drawing scale ✓ Drawing plans ✓ Drawing sections and views • Preparation of materials, tools and equipment ✓ Identification of ceiling materials ✓ Identification of tools used in ceiling ✓ Identification of equipment used in ceiling ✓ Selection of materials, tools and equipment • Applying safety precautions in working area ✓ Use Personal Protective Equipment ✓ Working area safety Sign posts Hazards and risks management

4 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation ✓ Cleaning the workplace Resources required for the indicative content Equipment • PPEs ,Circular saw ,Ladder/scaffolding, Air compressor, Band saw, Wheel barrow ,Surface planer ,Thicknesses planner, Belt sander, Grinder machine, Drilling machine, Nail gun, welding machine. Materials • Stucco, Gypsum compound, Paint, Wooden board , Acoustic tile, Gypsum, Plywood, PVC Panel, MDF, Nails, Warning tapes, Glue, Sanding papers, Screws , Bolt, Hinges , Locks, Varnish , Lacquer , Thinner, Galvanized wire, Water , PVC pipes, Scratching materials, cutting discs, electrodes, protective materials, fuels. Tools • Hammers, Hose pip, Building line, Carpenter’s bags, Measuring tape, Spirit level, Hand saws , Machete , Pencil/pen/mark pen, Folding rulers, Screw drivers, Spanners ,Hand planers , Squares , Brush , Chisels , Divider, Files, Rasp, Utility knife, Marking gauge , Painting roller Facilitation techniques Group discussion, individual activity • The trainer prepares a ceiling plan and asks students to discuss key elements to review when interpreting the plan. Afterward, the trainer asks them to interpret the ceiling plan based on their observations • The trainer gives a brief overview of the materials, tools, and equipment needed for ceiling installation, and involves trainees in selecting these items individually. • Trainer asks students site visit in the workshop or site for demonstrate the required functions of each tools and equipment used in ceiling installation and trainees prepare site visit report findings. • Trainer prepare the scenario about the activity conducted in ceiling construction, askes trainees to identify potential hazards and recommended PPE based on that activity. Formative assessment methods • Written assessment • Performance assessment • Oral assessment

5 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Learning outcome 2: Set out ceiling frame Learning hours: 15 hours Indicative content • Setting the reference line ✓ Description Methods of fixing reference line of ceiling ✓ Fixing reference line for ceiling ✓ Marking the reference line • Fixing the ceiling height ✓ Description of ceiling types ✓ Identify Standard height of ceiling ✓ Marking the height of ceiling • Levelling the ceiling frames ✓ Determine the level of ceiling frame ✓ Mark ceiling frame ✓ Alignment of ceiling frame ✓ Fix ceiling frame level Resources required for the indicative content Equipment • PPEs, Ladder/scaffolding, Air compressor, Band saw, Drilling machine, Nail gun, laser meter. Materials • Marker pen, chalk, nails, screws, welding rod Tools • Hammers, Hose pip, Building line, Carpenter’s bags, Measurin g tape, Spirit level, Pencil/pen/mark pen, Folding rulers, Screw drivers, Marking gauge , Painting roller Facilitation techniques • scenario, individual activity, group discussion • The trainer shows a video demonstrating the process of setting out a ceiling frame and divides the students into manageable groups, prompting them to discuss the steps involved in this process • Trainer demonstrate to the students on how to set out the reference line and trainer asks students to set reference line themselves. • Trainer demonstrate to the students to fix out ceiling height and trainer asks trainees to fix ceiling height themselves. • Trainer demonstrate to the students on how fix out ceiling height and trainer asks trainees to fix ceiling height themselves. • Trainer and trainees perform activity of levelling ceiling frame and trainer asks trainees to level ceiling frame themselves • Trainer provide students site visit ongoing project. Formative assessment methods • Written assessment • Performance assessment • Oral assessment

6 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Learning outcome 3: Construct Ceiling frame Learning hours: 20 hours Indicative content • Erect scaffolding ✓ Select scaffolding ✓ Protect the scaffolding lower part (base plate) ✓ Fix scaffolding parts • Identification of ceiling frame layout ✓ Parts of ceiling frame Runner Hanger Tie beam Struts ✓ Determine direction of ceiling joists ✓ Marking ceiling shape • Assembling wooden ceiling frame ✓ Fixing the perimeter wall joists ✓ Marking on perimeter wall joists ✓ Fixing the main runners ✓ Fixing cross tee ✓ Levelling the frame • Assembling metal /aluminium ceiling frame ✓ Fixing the perimeter wall joists ✓ Marking on perimeter wall joists ✓ Fixing the main runners ✓ Fixing the cross tee ✓ Levelling the frame Alignment with building lines Resources required for the indicative content Equipment ● Screw gun or drill, safety equipment (PPE) , welding machine Materials ● Chalk, charcoal, marker , pen/ ink pen, nails, screws , welding rod Tools ● Hammer , tape measure, laser or water level, screwdriver, T-Square Facilitation techniques Group discussion, scenario, simulation and individual activity ● Trainer displays a video on erecting scaffolding. In manageable groups the students. He/she asks to discuss on types, elements, characteristics of good scaffolding and scaffolding safety rules

7 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation ● Trainer provide layout and create scenario of ceiling frame. Individually prepare frame layout procedures/steps and make ceiling frame. ● Trainer prepare the field visit to the ongoing project site Formative assessment methods ● Written assessment ● Oral assessment ● Performance assessment Learning outcome 4: Install ceiling covering material Learning hours: 20 hours Indicative content • Cutting the ceiling panels ✓ Measuring and marking ✓ Cutting the panels ✓ Testing the fit • Fixing the ceiling panels ✓ Fixing method based on ceiling covers and frame materials Nails Bolts pins ✓ Install suspended tile ceiling Locate ceiling joists or support Install wall angle s Hang main runners Insert cross Tees Cut tiles for edge and obstacles Install ceiling tile Final checks ✓ Fixing panels on frame ✓ Fixing joint cover • Perform finishing works ✓ Apply finishing on plywood and wooden plank ceiling Varnishing

8 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Painting Staining ✓ Apply finishing on gypsum ceiling Plastering Molding and skirting Texturing Painting • Prepare the workplace ✓ Removal of waste materials ✓ Materials for cleaning workplace ✓ Apply cleaning methods By Water By Brush By Air compressor Resources required for the indicative content Equipment ● Paint sprayer , Compressor , PPE , Drilling machine, Screw gun , Jig saw, Router machine Materials ● Thinner, Masking tape, varnish, paint, Sandpaper, Wood, Screws, Nails, Acoustic ceiling panels, Plywood, wall angles, cross tees, toile ceiling, hanging wires, suspended tile panel. Tools ● bucket, Tape measure, Drawing set, Spirit levels, Notebook, Screw driver, Hand saw, Plumb bob, Hammer, Try-square, Building line, knife cutter. Facilitation techniques Simulation and individual activity ● Trainer shows step by step how to cut and fix ceiling covering using actual materials and tools. This can be done in person or through video demonstration. He/she asks individually to cut and fix ceiling covers. And provide detailed instruction and guidance as students work through the cutting ● Trainer demonstrates the ceiling finishing through video or done in person and asks individually to apply finishing. He/she provide detailed instruction and guidance as students work through fixing process. ● Trainer allows students to practice installing ceilings covering and make finishing themselves under supervision. Formative assessment methods ● Oral assessment ● Written assessment ● Performance assessment

The company would like to hire ceiling installer to perform ceiling activities for the suite room to improve the room that will be warm, welcoming and reflect the charm of Nyanza District. As a ceiling installer, you are requested to perform the following tasks: 1. Set out ceiling frame 2. Install ceiling frame, from longitudinal to transversal sides of room. 3. Apply ceiling covering materials 4. Ceiling plan, materials, tools and equipment are available on site. 5. Activivities will be performed in 8 hours. 1 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Purpose statement This module describes the skills, knowledge and attitudes required to integrate learners/trainees in workplace for an industrial attachment program to gain work-based experience for future employment. The module will enable the learner/trainees to Demonstrate supervisory skills , enhance innovation during IAP and to promote professional skills transfer. Delivery modality Training delivery 100% Assessment Total 100% Theoretical content 30% Formative assessment 30% 100% Practical work: 70% 70% • Group project and presentation 20% • Individual project /Work 50% Summative Assessment N.A Elements of Competency and Performance Criteria Elements of competency Performance criteria 1. Demonstrate supervisory skills 1.1. Labour contracts are correctly developed based on labour market law 1.2. Supervisor roles and responsibilities are properly fulfilled based on organisation structure. 1.3. Supervisor qualities and skills are accurately exhibited at the workplace. 1.4. Document related to the work are appropriately filed. 2. Enhance creativity and innovation during IAP program 2.1. Innovation concepts are properly explained based on industrial attachment program core values. 2.2. Innovation strategies during industrial attachment program are properly described based on assigned industry duties. 2.3. Innovation process is effectively integrated in line with industrial attachment program program. 3. Promote and implement professional skills transfer 3.1. Implementation plan of competencies acquired during industrial attachment program is properly elaborated in accordance with labour market needs. 3.2. Knowledge, skills and attitudes acquired during industrial attachment program are effectively applied based on developed implementation plan. 3.3. Industrial attachment program report presentation is properly performed. se content

2 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Learning outcomes At the end of the module the learner will be able to: 1. Demonstrate supervisory skills 2. Enhance creativity and innovation during industrial attachment program 3. Promote professional skills transfer Learning outcome 1: Demonstrate supervisory skills Learning hours: 15 Indicative content • Identification of labour contract ✓ Definition of key terms Labor Contract Labor market ✓ Main components of labor contract Client Contractor duration ✓ Types of labor contract permanent labor contracts fixed-term contracts casual labor contracts ✓ Low governing contract in Rwanda • Identification of supervisor ’s roles and responsibilities ✓ Supervisor responsibilities Workflow management Trainning new employees/intern Creating team schedule Evaluating employee/interns performance ✓ Supervisor’s roles • Supervisor qualities and skills ✓ Meaning of key terms Skills Knowledge Qualities ✓ Supervisor skills Time management Communication skills Critical thinking ✓ Supervisor qualities Managing workflow Trainning new hires

3 | P a g e Employable Skills for Sustainable Job Creation Creating and managing team schedules Reporting Evaluating performance and providing feed back Help in employees conflict resolution • Filing work related documents ✓ Definition of key terms Filing File document ✓ Different ways to file documents in a filing cabinet Alphabetical Category of Date Numerical Combination Resources required for the learning outcome Equipment • Computer ,projector ,chalk board ,Flipchart stand Materials • Markers, chalks, pen, Scotch tape, Papers, flip chat Tools • Labor contract sample • Visual aids Facilitation techniques • Demonstration and simulation • Individual research • Group discussion and presentation • Learning through interaction of guest speakers(Practitioners) • Learning through visits on the relevant institutions • Case study Formative assessment methods • Written assessment • Oral presentation • Performance assessment

The Management of Technological Innovation: Strategy and Practice. Completely rev. and updated. Oxford: Oxford University Press 2.
